0.long_answer: Oculofaciocardiodental syndrome is caused by lesions in the BCOR gene, which is located on the short arm of the X chromosome at the Xp11.4 position. Mutations in the BCOR gene affect the production of the BCL6 corepressor protein, leading to the clinical manifestations of the condition.
